name: ARM Cortex Debug 10-pin (SWD/JTAG)
description: The ARM standard 10-pin debug connector for Cortex-M (and others). Carries Serial Wire Debug (SWDIO/SWCLK) with optional trace (SWO), or full JTAG on the same pins (TMS/TCK/TDO/TDI). Used by ST-Link, J-Link, DAPLink, the Pi Pico debug probe, and the Bus Pirate's SWD mode. Pin 1 (VTref) senses the target's logic voltage so the probe level-shifts correctly.

contacts.name: VTref
contacts.description: target reference voltage -- the probe reads this to set its I/O level (does not power the target)

contacts.name: SWO/TDO
contacts.description: Serial Wire Output trace / JTAG TDO (optional)

contacts.name: KEY
contacts.description: keyed / no pin (shroud alignment); leave unconnected

contacts.name: NC/TDI
contacts.description: not connected on pure SWD; JTAG TDI when doing full JTAG

contacts.name: nRESET
contacts.description: target reset, active low (optional but recommended for connect-under-reset)

variants: The 20-pin ARM JTAG connector (0.1-inch) is the older/full variant with all JTAG signals + more grounds; a 20-to-10 adapter is common.
SWD uses only VTref, SWDIO, SWCLK, GND (+ optional SWO and nRESET). Full JTAG additionally uses TDO/TDI (pins 6/8).
gotchas: Pin 1 (VTref) is a SENSE input, not a supply -- it does not power the target. The target must be powered separately; VTref just tells the probe whether it's a 3.3 V or 1.8 V part.
For a chip that has re-purposed its SWD pins as GPIO in firmware (common on STM32/nRF), you need connect-under-reset: hold nRESET (pin 10) low while the probe attaches, or it can't get in.
The 0.05-inch (1.27 mm) fine-pitch version and the 0.1-inch version share the pinout but need the matching cable/connector -- don't force a 0.1-inch IDC onto a fine-pitch footprint.
notes: ARM Cortex Debug 10-pin standard (SWD + optional JTAG/SWO). Pin order per the ARM connector spec.
